clue.text: No playing with his food, Orsino, for such a lover?

definitions.text: No playing with his food, Orsino, for such a lover?

parts.words: No playing with his food, Orsino, for such a lover
parts.note: Orsino in Twelfth Night opens with 'If music be the food of love, play on'; a lover with no ear for music would refuse that food

explanation.surface: A fussy diner is told not to play with his food, addressed to Shakespeare's lovesick duke.
explanation.walkthrough: Orsino is the duke in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night whose first line calls music the food of love. A lover who will not 'play on' with that food has no feeling for music.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with no taste or talent for melody would refuse Orsino's musical diet of love.

clue.text: Minimum price of staging a film on Everest?

explanation.surface: An auction reserve seems to be the fee for shooting a movie on the world's highest mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: At auction the lowest price a seller will accept is the 'upset price'. Read as two words, a film set placed on Everest is a set put up high.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction's reserve figure is called the upset price; a film set raised high on a mountain is a set placed up aloft.

clue.text: Wind of a base revolutionary uprising ?

parts.note: base in the sense of low or ignoble means mean

indicators.note: in a down clue, an uprising lifts the word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a revolutionary is a Red, a communist

explanation.surface: A breeze stirs during a lowly insurrection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' is the verb (rhymes with 'find'), as a river winds. 'uprising' turns RED upwards to DER after MEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander in loops, as a river does along its valley, is to twist and turn.

clue.text: Something for Nurse Wolf to arrange in a vase

definitions.text: Something for Nurse Wolf to arrange in a vase

indicators.note: arranging the letters of the two names puts them into a new order, as flowers are arranged

explanation.surface: A nurse called Wolf has some blooms to put in a vase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to arrange' does double duty in the surface (flower arranging) and the wordplay: the letters of NURSE WOLF rearrange into the answer, and the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall yellow bloom with a dark centre is the kind of cut flower one puts in a vase.

clue.text: An abundance of foot trouble among the Pyramids

parts.note: a corn is a painful hard patch of skin on the foot
among here gives the small word in
the Pyramids stand in Egypt, so they stand for the country

explanation.surface: A tourist among the Pyramids suffers from plenty of sore feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corn in Egypt' is a stock phrase for plenty, from the Genesis story of Joseph storing grain in Egypt during famine.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical grain stored up by Joseph became a byword for plenty, a great store of anything.

clue.text: Old timer would cause delay

explanation.surface: An elderly clock is said to make things late.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'old lag' is a convict who has served much time, so a timer is someone doing time, not a clock. The second sense is a time lag, a delay.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict who has done time inside is a lag; an interval of hold-up is a time lag.

clue.text: Heroic tales ? It's a lot of vain talk

parts.note: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
gas is empty boastful chatter

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses grand epics as so much hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is the 1920s word for sex appeal, SA, a crossword convention; ''s' is a link (is).
explanation.definitionFit: Norse and Icelandic prose epics about heroes and families are the original long tales of this kind.

clue.text: Charmer letting off steam ?

explanation.surface: A seductive person seems to be venting frustration.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the sea nymph of myth whose song lured sailors; the second is a steam-driven warning whistle, which works by releasing steam.
explanation.definitionFit: A seductive woman is called after the singing nymphs of Greek myth; a ship's or factory's hooter blows by releasing steam.

clue.text: Old heavyweight involved in a light round

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A veteran heavyweight boxer takes part in a bout against a lighter opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles A LIGHT together with O (round) to make the giant. The boxing picture of heavyweight and round is false.
explanation.definitionFit: The Philistine giant felled by David's sling in the Bible is the original heavyweight of ancient times.

clue.text: Do its members pay now, spend later? Or vice versa ?

definitions.text: Do its members pay now, spend later? Or vice versa

parts.words: Do its members pay now, spend later? Or vice versa
parts.note: a savings club whose members pay in weekly and draw out at Christmas, while 'on the slate' means on credit, buying now and paying later

explanation.surface: A puzzled observer asks how a club's members manage their money.
explanation.walkthrough: A British slate club was a workplace or pub savings club paying out at Christmas; 'put it on the slate' means buy on credit, hence 'or vice versa'.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional British savings society collected small weekly sums and shared them out at year's end.

clue.text: Works troublemaker

parts.note: a tool that, thrown into machinery, wrecks it, from the idiom about sabotaging the works

explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like a factory with a militant shop steward, but it is the idiom 'a ___ in the works', a tool jamming machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for sabotage names the wrench thrown into the works of a machine.

clue.text: Animal from a stream 'in Indian territory

indicators.note: in places the stream inside the Indian state

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast, once Portuguese
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A creature emerges from a brook in a region of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts RILL inside GOA. 'Animal' is the definition; 'from a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of the great apes is an animal native to African forests.

clue.text: The attractions of these waters are out of this world

definitions.text: The attractions of these waters are out of this world

parts.words: The attractions of these waters are out of this world
parts.note: the waters are pulled by the moon, a literal attraction from beyond the earth

explanation.walkthrough: 'out of this world' looks like praise for a beauty spot, but the attraction is gravity: the moon draws the sea in its rise and fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Waters that rise and fall twice daily are drawn by the pull of moon and sun.

clue.text: Hint that Auntie's in trouble

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Someone suggests that an aunt has got herself into difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges AUNTIES IN; 'that' links. The surface reads 'in trouble' together, but 'in' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To suggest something indirectly, without saying it outright, is to imply it.

clue.text: In which role Lady Macbeth had a spot of bother

definitions.text: In which role Lady Macbeth had a spot of bother

parts.words: In which role Lady Macbeth had a spot of bother
parts.note: in the night scene she wanders unconscious, scrubbing at an imagined bloodstain and crying 'Out, damned spot!'

explanation.walkthrough: 'a spot of bother' is British understatement for trouble, but here the spot is the imagined blood on her hands in Macbeth's night-walking scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Macbeth walks and talks in her slumber, revealing her guilt to a doctor and gentlewoman.

clue.text: It's steep, this rent should come down with a rush

definitions.text: this rent should come down with a rush

explanation.surface: A landlord's charge is high and ought to fall quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a steep rocky hill, as on Dartmoor. Put the answer before 'rent' and you get a torrent, which comes down with a rush.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocky peak on the moors rises sharply; joined to 'rent' it makes a rushing stream.

clue.text: This won't perhaps accommodate rustics

parts.note: a city residence is not where country folk would live, as opposed to a country house

explanation.walkthrough: The urban home of a family with a country seat; rustics belong in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: An urban terrace residence is the opposite of a farmhouse for country people.

clue.text: Means to reverse the law about the place of enclosures

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the reversed word goes round the other piece
to reverse something is to turn it back, so the word for the law is read backwards

parts.note: taken as the word law
a letter's enclosures come with it; the formal word 'herewith' marks where they are sent along

explanation.surface: A lawyer's ploy is to overturn the rules governing fenced-in land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reverse' turns LAW to WAL, and 'about' wraps WAL round HEREWITH, the business-letter word for 'enclosed with this'.
explanation.definitionFit: The money or resources needed for a purpose are the means to do it.

clue.text: Like Fleet Street on Christmas Day without children ?

definitions.text: Like Fleet Street on Christmas Day

explanation.surface: London's newspaper district is quiet on December 25th, with no youngsters about.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street was the home of London's national newspapers, which printed no edition on Christmas Day. 'Issue' also means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: With no edition printed, the papers have nothing out that day; a couple with no offspring has no heirs.

clue.text: Girls fluent in classical literature

parts.note: fluent in its root sense of flowing: maidens of Greek myth living in streams and springs

explanation.walkthrough: 'fluent' looks like skill in Latin and Greek, but it means flowing: the naiads of classical myth live in rivers and fountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Naiads of Greek legend are female spirits of springs, rivers and lakes.

clue.text: The number heading island rising can be defended

indicators.note: heading means coming first, so the number goes on top of the other piece in this down clue

parts.note: the number ten

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising turns the island's name to read upwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island where Napoleon was exiled

explanation.surface: A tally sits at the top of an island that is rebelling and holding out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses ELBA to ABLE, and 'heading' puts TEN above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A position that can be held against attack is defensible.

clue.text: O.T. workman

parts.note: the Old Testament patriarch whose name is spelt like a piece of work

explanation.walkthrough: O.T. is the Old Testament, home of the long-suffering patriarch; spelt the same, a piece of work is what a workman does.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffering patriarch of the Old Testament shares his name's spelling with a task or piece of work.

clue.text: Snug work

parts.note: work that fits snugly together: the craft of fitting wood with tight joints

explanation.walkthrough: 'Snug' suggests a cosy pub room, but here it means a close fit, as wooden joints should be.
explanation.definitionFit: The carpenter's craft of making tight-fitting wooden doors, frames and fittings is close-fitting woodwork.

clue.text: She's sadly miscast in theatre production

indicators.note: a part badly cast is put in the wrong place, so the letters are wrongly placed
a production stages something afresh, so the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: An actress has been badly miscast in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly miscast' and 'production' together rearrange IN THEATRE into a girl's name; ''s' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, the feminine form of Henry, stands for any 'she'.

clue.text: Unsuitable fresh paint

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A decorator calls wet paint inappropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges PAINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not apt or fitting for its purpose is inappropriate.

clue.text: The Dictator's internal decree

indicators.note: internal means inside, so the letters are found within the clue's words

explanation.surface: A dictator issues a domestic order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'internal' points to letters within THE DICTATOR'S.
explanation.definitionFit: An official order issued by a ruler or authority is a decree.

clue.text: A sense in which the last scene's lacking, said Jaques

definitions.text: in which the last scene's lacking, said Jaques

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's melancholy courtier says the final act lacks something.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaques in As You Like It ends his Seven Ages of Man speech with 'Last scene of all ... sans teeth, sans eyes, sans taste, sans everything'.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five senses is the one the tongue serves; old age in Jaques's speech is without it.

clue.text: Reproach in hair-raising' fashion ?

explanation.surface: A scolding is delivered in a terrifying manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hair-raising' suggests fright, but read literally, hair raised up in a plait is up in a braid.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold or reprove sharply; split into two words it is hair lifted up and plaited.

clue.text: Douse the glim !

parts.note: old slang for 'put out the light', an order a driver obeys by lowering the headlights

explanation.walkthrough: 'Glim' is old slang for a light; drivers lower headlights to stop dazzling oncoming traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower car headlamps so they do not dazzle is to dim their beam.

clue.text: Rings for retainers

explanation.surface: Rings are worn by servants.
explanation.walkthrough: A keeper is a ring worn to hold a more valuable ring on the finger; keepers are also custodians or guards.
explanation.definitionFit: Guard rings hold a wedding band in place; guardians or custodians hold things in their charge.

clue.text: Leave the river at last

indicators.note: last means coming at the end, so the small word follows the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Someone finally departs the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' places AT after EXE. 'Leave' is the noun: an exeat is permission for a pupil to be away from school.
explanation.definitionFit: A school's permission for a boarder to be absent is a formal leave of absence.

clue.text: For Fay, the point of writing for the 'columns

parts.note: fay is an old word for a fairy, and a peri is a fairy of Persian legend
a style is a pointed instrument for writing on wax tablets, a stylus

explanation.surface: A writer called Fay explains her aim in writing newspaper columns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fay' looks like a woman's name but is the old word for a fairy; 'columns' are pillars, not newspaper pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of pillars surrounding a courtyard or temple is a colonnade.
